description: NovaBeam OS AURA Planet X / SPHEREx Hunter uses NASA SPHEREx observations to search for moving objects and unusual changes in the sky. AURA compares observation epochs, creates difference images, ranks candidates, and checks them against known Solar System objects. Developed by Tyrone M. Sanders, Co-founder of House of the QR Code™, the project explores how AI can assist astronomical discovery.
summary:
NovaBeam OS AURA — Planet X / SPHEREx Hunter

Creator and Software Developer: Tyrone M. Sanders  
Organization: House of the QR Code™  
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — San Jose, California

NovaBeam OS AURA is an interactive astronomical research application developed for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It explores how infrared sky-survey information can support research into Planet Nine, a hypothetical planet beyond Neptune.

The browser-based application features an interactive research dashboard, survey exploration, quality screening, candidate-region analysis, scientific visualization, and JSON report exports.

During prototype testing, the research workflow produced 45,750 quality-screened samples and identified six regions for further investigation. These are preliminary computational results, not confirmed planetary detections. No verified moving-object tracks have been established.

The project emphasizes accessible astronomical research, transparent reporting, and responsible scientific interpretation.

Future development may include cross-survey comparisons, improved screening methods, and independent validation.

Developed by Tyrone M. Sanders with AI-assisted coding and documentation support.
details:
NovaBeam OS AURA — Planet X / SPHEREx Hunter is a browser-based astronomical research application created by Tyrone M. Sanders of House of the QR Code™ for NASA Space Apps 2026.

Using NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 infrared survey observations, the application searches sky regions, loads spectral-image data, aligns observations from two dates, screens image-quality flags and variance, compares image differences, and exports structured JSON reports.

A November 15 prototype report records 45,750 quality-screened samples, 385 high-residual samples, and six unverified regions for further investigation. These are preliminary image differences, not confirmed moving-object tracks or discoveries of Planet Nine. Independent verification remains necessary.

Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, AURA offers an interactive research dashboard that makes survey exploration more accessible. Its goals are transparent reporting, reproducible analysis, and responsible interpretation of NASA open data. The concept, creative direction, testing, and final decisions belong to Tyrone M. Sanders; ChatGPT assisted with coding, debugging, and documentation.
